text:
Recent research supports separating sampled-ranking performance, representation geometry, and sequence sensitivity. [RecSys 2025](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086) finds that logging and negative-sampling choices affect evaluation reliability; [2024 rank-estimation research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371) likewise documents sampling bias. For this benchmark, retain the fixed 99-negative HR@10 protocol. Proposed diagnostics: positive rank, number of sampled negatives outranking it, and rank distance from the top-10 cutoff—interpretable alternatives to absolute score-margin thresholds. Audit full-catalog unseen-item rankings separately; unobserved items are not verified negatives, and recommendation diversity is not evidence of accuracy.

[RankMe](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.02885) defines effective rank as exp(−Σ pᵢ log pᵢ), with pᵢ proportional to singular values. [ICML 2024](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/guo24e.html) links embedding collapse to limited recommendation-model scalability. Measure item embeddings and user representations separately, document centering and sample size, exclude padding/mask tokens, and report effective rank relative to attainable rank. These findings do not establish a universal collapse threshold or prove that effective rank predicts BERT4Rec HR@10 failures.

[2024 sequence-shuffling research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.12008) motivates sensitivity probes: perturb only diagnostic history copies, preserve padding and appended-mask readout, and measure changes in representations and candidate ranks. Proposed uncertainty analysis, consistent with [distribution-aware evaluation](https://841.io/doc/disteval.html): bootstrap users within each category, preserve pairing for model comparisons, and recompute the four-category macro-average. These intervals condition on the fixed candidates; they omit candidate-sampling and training-seed uncertainty. Validate diagnostic usefulness through category-specific associations with observed validation misses, without fitting additional predictors or treating exploratory associations as established causes.
